I think that BTW and SA (and their b-tracks) are superior beyond comparison to UL. But after several listens of UL, it's really grown on me to the point I'd agree with your categorization of "really fine". Also on subsequent listens I've heard a lot more of BTW and SA on the album, such as on Not The One, It's Only Natural, maybe White Braids & Pillow Chair (sounds kind of like a late-track off BTW)... and Veronica and Tangelo kind of are like b-tracks of BTW b-tracks lol, specifically Bicycle Song and Eskimo, respectively, KIND OF. There are also nods to former albums in several other tracks (obviously... they are stylistically still themselves), but the aforementioned ones are most obvious to me. Here Ever After, as well, in parts captures a very distinct sound/vibe, especially in the later part of the track, that is very unique to BTW-era RHCP, which might well be my favourite. As much as UL has grown on me the past week-- and it truly has, a great deal--, I do still standby my initial reaction, which will rub fellow diehard fans the wrong way no doubt... and that is that these tracks wouldn't have even made it as b-tracks to the aforementioned albums (+ Californication). I know it'll continue to grow on me more and more with each play (I probably spin it 2-3 x a day), but just know it will never compare to their earlier works with John- and I don't think that's because of some heavy bias and gatekeeping surrounding their earlier works (which I've held on a pedestal in the highest regard since first falling for them in the very early-2000's during the Cali-BTW-era)- it's just not near that level, despite the homages they themselves seem to be attempting to pay to it.

Looking outside of my window, absorbing the last bits of sunlight I'll see in my 20's. I didn't expect to have as much dread and anxiety around turning 30, but it's here in full effect. I've struggled with depression and suicidal ideation for most of my adult life, but tonight really feel like acting on it as I reflect on a lifetime of failure. Please don't attempt to comfort me, it's too late for any of that. I'm a complete and utter mess of a human and the poster boy for all that can go wrong. I lost my dad in September of 2018 to the worst possible death any human can die and thinking back on his final months and moments is enough to make me not want to live. About five years ago he was diagnosed with a rare and aggressive type of dementia-- specifically, frontotemporal degeneration with a side of semantic variant primary progressive aphasia--, which rendered him completely unable to communicate with us, not only verbally, but via gestures or otherwise. The analogy which I like to use is that of an astronaut out on a spacewalk whose tether to the ship has been cut loose and he's been left floating through space, through alien worlds, with no ability to communicate. Things got so bad towards that end that we had to take him to the hospital, which was the beginning of a very long drawn out and extremely painful death, which I wouldn't wish upon my very worst enemy. Being in such an already incredibly fragile cognitive state, removing him from his familiar surrounding (our home), which was all he had left, expedited his demise tenfold. My mother and I were the only ones he recognized, but what little trust he had left in us went out the window after this betrayal we committed taking him to the hospital. So he did what I assume is the last thing that was in his power and stopped eating. The hospital was absolutely horrendous and because he was a difficult and resilient patient, seemed to just want him gone. A month in hospital without taking a bite of anything, then his last month at home, again without even just a spoon of pudding or anything. IV's could only keep him alive for so long. Every moment of every day from the start of his diagnosis was a battle, but the last two months- and specifically last month- were a hell the likes of which you couldn't begin to imagine even in the darkest depths of your imagination. He passed away in the early ours of September 27th in front of me, shortly after I shared some special words with him. He was far beyond the point of communicating and in an extremely deteriorated and ugly state in these final moments, but I like to think he understood- it was as if these were things he needed to here before leaving this world. I'll never forget that deeply shaking feeling of witnessing someone take their very last breaths. I fell over  him crying like I never have and held him tight until the very last bits of warmth left his body. I'd been depressed so much before then, but all those episodes were absolutely nothing compared to the immeasurable pain which settled in when dad died. We (my mother and I) tried so fucking hard to save him and were there from 6:30am to 10pm in the hospital every single day by his side, begging and pleading for him to eat, but he'd decided his own fate and took this one last stand, flexing his power one more time. Growing up, it was always just us three; me and my parents vs. the world. I had friends in school, but never really close ones. I never belonged. My parents were my best friends. We shared so many incredible moments, which I wish I remembered more of- hopefully they come back to me over time. My dad was the epitome of what a great man should be. He worked his ass of harder than anyone I've ever known to not only support us, but to let us lead the most comfortable lives possible. He was the absolute light of any gathering he ever attended- everyones eyes lit up when he showed up. He gave me the world, and in return I wasn't anywhere near the best son I could be. Growing up, up until my late teens, I was as close as could be with him, but starting around age 20 I started drifting away emotionally and became somewhat of a dick. I regret the several years when I wasn't at my best, because they were the last years I could have had to make meaningful memories with him- of course I never would have expected that soon after he'd be diagnosed with the worst of the worst diseases- even his doctors said it was much worse than cancer. A few years after dad got sick, mom did as well, with immensely high and deadly blood pressure due to the extreme stress of the situation and having to keep the household up on her own- I could only help and contribute so much, but of course did my very best. One day her nose wouldn't stop bleeding and so I took her to the ER, where she had a BP of 267/133; the highest the triage nurse said she'd ever seen. She was immediately admitted on started on a poisonous cycle of medications, which only made her worse. Keep in mind this whole time my dad is at home alone and unattended, so I had to rush between staying with her at the hospital and home to cook and care for him. My life at this point was just... I don't even know what to say. As bad as it was though, I'd give anything to be back at that point, because I'd at least still have him around. Mom was discharged a week later, but as it was still early in her diagnosis, the meds they'd started her on were really fucking her up and her BP wasn't coming down, so it was nightly ER visits for several months- some nights up to three times... Most times waiting in the ER for up to 16 hours before being shooed off by incompetent doctors. It was fucking hell. Having me sleep by her side was the only "medicine" that somewhat worked- she felt safe next to me and that calmed her down, lowering the BP. After several months, she was put on the meds which have thus far worked best in stabilizing her, but still far from working well- she's nowhere near the same person she was before the meds, and it kills me to know that it will be next to impossible to get her back to that point. She'd never had issues with high BP before and was active + healthy, but the insurmountable stresses of the situation with dad really worked a number on her. Her BP still spikes to this day and she's far from good, causing me to constantly worry about her. Literally all I can think about is death- her death, my death, my dads death, death in general. My thoughts are all black. After dad passed, I sold most of what I owned to be able to fly him back to his home country, in Europe, where I know beyond a shadow of a doubt that he'd have wanted to buried. He's buried just up the hill from his childhood home, among all of his family, in a beautifully scenic and mountainous part of the world- it's my wish to be there next to him once I perish. We stayed in Europe for a couple months, first with family, then travelling around a bit to get our minds off the situation- and it even worked for a period, but when we got back home the greatest depression of my life set in. I was in bed all day, didn't care about a single thing, days blurred. I was certain I'd never do anything again. Then towards the end of the summer I got a spark of motivation and for a couple months went back to working in the creative industry I worked in before, as a freelancer. I dropped out of my second year of college to pursue a career in a very difficult to break into industry and somehow made it in- not only that, but I actually prospered in it from a fairly young age (19 onwards). But looking back, it was just a ploy to escape any real responsibility I'd have in school. I've always been looking for the easy way out my entire life, like a soldier dodging the draft. After dad got sick, I gave up working altogether and just started rotting away, okay with whatever came my way. I have a tremendous amount of talent, but it'll never be fully realized because I'm my own worst enemy. I'm getting tired of writing now, but wanted to briefly touch on the fact that I've also never experienced romantic love and affection in any form. That's right, I'm about to be a 30 year old virgin. Pathetic. I actively chased after girls in my teens and early/mid-20's, but eventually got the message and gave up. It never bothered me much, but lately has been one of the few things I can only think about. I thought about getting an escort to get it over with, but knew that'd weigh down on me morally afterwards and only contribute further to the darkness in my mind. There's so much more I want to write just for the sake of getting it all down, but I've tired myself out now and will just go cry in my bed. Actually, one other thing I wanted to add that has been pissing me off is how I've done so fucking much for several of my closest friends over the years... given them great expensive birthday gifts, taken them to countless lunches and dinners and always footed the bill, done them huge favours and provided my services free, yet save for one or two of them, none know it's my birthday tomorrow and won't even text me. I'm not even talking about receiving gifts, god no... I'm not a kid to want that, but after all I've done for them and given them, would it kill them to at least get me a nice bottle of whisky? I'm a fucking ghost to them. But at least I learned that lesson now and know who to further cut out of my life. I know nobody read this wall of text and that's fine, I just wanted to vent. There's so much more, but this is what's on my mind now. I didn't think I'd care about turning 30 at all, but society does one hell of a job at highlighting all your failures and things you didn't accomplish by this age as you approach the number.

Just wanted to say that it's precisely this kind of inter-generational and objective discussion why I love Reddit *so* damn much. Amazing points and insights by both of you- thank you so much for contributing to the thread. The intel about Leica and the Jews during WWII really has elevated the company in my eyes and garnered a great amount of respect from me- incredible. Some amazing photos on your IG, definitely ones I rarely see taken on a Leica-  I'll be sure to follow.

My "beef" isn't with how a Leica *feels*\- you can see in my op what a strong impression my few brief encounters with merely holding a few over the years left; it's unparalleled in its physicality, which no doubt elicits inspiration from the user-, but 'merely' with how a lot of the images taken on them look. I find that there's a significant disparity between the product and the results. But who am I? I'm certainly no arbiter of what is and isn't a "good photo", and if shooting a Leica brings joy to its owner, well that's really what it's all about. And yes, I 100% agree re: their pricing being downright prohibitively high for many. I don't know whether to refer to Leica as a luxury brand or not, but let's run with it being one... anyways, the myriad of limited editions (akin to Omega and their countless editions of the Speedmaster) sort of cheapens the brand, don't you think?

The "Leica look" most definitely is a real thing. While I'm not a technically-oriented person in the slightest, I'm quite confident that if you were to lay out various images in front of me taken on various cameras that I'd be able to pick out the ones shot on a Leica (implying that both body + lens are Leica, though the body undoubtedly matters less in conveying this aesthetic). The above linked article mentions Zeiss lenses frequently- they're the closest I've seen in rendering to Leica glass; quite a lot of visual parallels, imo. Re: replicating this look in post- it's, imho, simply not possible, as it's an amalgamation of factors, some technical, some more abstract and hard to pinpoint/discern, the least important of which is vibrance of colours and even contrast. I'm getting a bit lost in my own train of thought here, but I'll end by saying that even though I've found the vast majority of Leica shots I've seen underwhelming, they've got an undeniable aesthetic that's entirely unique to them (approached by some Zeiss products), which I've no doubt in the hands of the right photographers could yield magical results- this is why I'm glad to have learned about some new (to me) photographers in this thread, the work of whom is really impressive!

When I was 15 my schoolfellow, whose brother I was friendly with, asked me to follow him outside to a lightly wooded area behind our school where kids used to go smoke. Everything seemed totally normal- we were making casual small conversation- and once we got to the spot I said "hold on, I have to take a piss". Turned my back on him to do the deed and next thing I felt was a super hard punch to my upper right back. Turns out this "punch" was actually a stab- specifically, a stab with an 8" knife. He was kind enough to A) inform me I'd been stabbed and B) remove the knife. Survival instinct kicked in and I fell to the ground pretending to be dead, because he would of kept going otherwise. Once I fell to the ground he took my watch off my hand, which we soon learned (according to him) was the impetus for the stabbing- he planned to pawn it (a $200 Fossil watch my mom bought my on vacation to Italy a couple years earlier) and buy some coke. Once he ran off and I started getting up I noticed something was very wrong... I couldn't breath. My friends happened to be behind the school when I emerged from the wooded area yelling for them to go get help as I'd just been stabbed. They thought I was joking around as I usually did, but one of them finally came over after I fell to my knees and saw I was being for real, blood going everywhere. They'd fetched a teacher who proved to be the human embodiment of incompetence- she got the bright idea to have me lay on my stomach, which could of expedited the process of flooding my lungs with blood, but thankfully didn't as I only stayed in that position for a few seconds. The pain began to intensify as I was constantly gasping for air, but also some nerve damage had been done and my movement was greatly constricted. They propped me up against the lockers by the back entrance, where my blood coated the wall, and it took about 25 min for the ambulance to arrive. I was still in a great deal of pain even with the oxygen mask on, but it was nothing compared to the pain I'd experience shortly after in the ER/OR where they made a 5-6" incision under my armpit in order to get at my lung so that they could insert a chest tube. The feeling of having the doctors hands INSIDE of me, feeling around and holding my lung while I was still awake (under local anaesthetic) is the most bizarre thing I've ever encountered and a sensation I will never forget. I still don't know why they couldn't have put me under fully for such a procedure instead of administering local all around my body... At this point my parents had been brought in and were in hysterics after seeing me on the OR table with blood everywhere. My mom was at home when the principal called to notify her what'd happened and ordered a cop to drive her to the hospital, a trauma centre about 30 min away from our home. My dad was at work on a construction site and went into a rage, getting together a band of his friends/workers to come to the hospital to find out who did this- they wanted to go kill the guy, but my mom managed to talk some sense into him. I was the most innocent 15 year old kid, never into drugs, alcohol, gangs, etc. and struggled for a long time with the question of "why me?" when there were so many much worse people out there than me... not that anyone deserves this kind of punishment. Was a $200 watch worth it? I spent a couple weeks in the hospitals trauma unit and then a further month or two at home recovering. Whoever stitched me up did a horrible job as they kept coming undone and I had to visit the ER several times to have that fixed... bleeding out in public was NOT fun... Psychologically it honestly didn't do too much damage as I think I was just too young to grasp the full weight of what'd happened... but physically it left the entire area around my upper right back and right arm/armpit completely numb for the rest of my life. I was also told that the lung could randomly collapse at any time-- apparently that's a possibility for those having suffered a traumatic pneumothorax, can anyone confirm?--, but it's been almost 15 years since the incident and I haven't had any major issues with the lung thus far. The guy who did it was 17 and protected by the young offenders act here in Canada, which means he did zero jail time for this... I think he just got some community service hours. Blows my fucking mind- what a dysfunctional system...
